component.title: Quanta Celestial Peak FPGA Test SOP

steps.title: Verify Preconditions
steps.subtitle: Prepare the tester and confirm required access before starting.
items: Confirm the tester is powered on and has completed boot-up.
Confirm PuTTY access is available and the Linux root shell can be reached.
Record the tester or unit identifier using the local production process.
steps.warning: Do not begin if approved tester access or identification is unavailable.

steps.title: Verify BMC and BIOS
steps.subtitle: Both firmware versions must match the controlled requirement exactly.
items: Required BMC: C2390.BC.0310.00
Required BIOS: C2390.BS.3A10.GN1
Check the BMC in the management interface or system information page.
Check the BIOS in BIOS Setup or the available system information page.
steps.warning: If either version differs, stop and follow the approved firmware update process before continuing.

steps.title: Connect to the Tester
steps.subtitle: Open PuTTY and verify the Linux root prompt.
items: Start PuTTY and connect using the approved tester connection information.
Log in and confirm the root shell prompt is available: root@localhost:~#.
steps.warning: Capture the exact connection error before escalating an access problem.

steps.title: Load the Catapult Driver
steps.subtitle: Load the required FPGA card driver from the root shell.
items: Run: modprobe catapult
Confirm the command completes without an error.
The console may identify catapult.ko driver version v5.32.1.1.
steps.warning: Stop and capture the exact message if modprobe reports an error.

steps.title: Detect the FPGA
steps.subtitle: List the installed FPGA and record its actual chip ID.
items: Run: fpgadiagnostics -list
Confirm the utility reports: Found 1 FPGAs.
Copy the complete numeric value shown in the Chip ID column.
Check that no digits are missing or added.
steps.warning: The example chip ID in the SOP is not universal. Always use the chip ID returned by the current tester.

steps.title: Load the Application Image
steps.subtitle: Reconfigure the detected FPGA to application flash slot 1.
items: Run: fpgadiagnostics -chip <CHIP_ID> -reconfigApp
Replace <CHIP_ID> with the full numeric value returned by fpgadiagnostics -list.
Allow the command to disable and re-enable PCIe devices, reload the flash image, and retrain the PCIe link.
steps.warning: Do not interrupt the command and do not substitute the example chip ID from the document.

steps.title: Verify Reconfiguration
steps.subtitle: Confirm all required success indicators before continuing.
items: Found management function. Search complete.
Found role function. Search complete.
PCIe link retrained to gen3x8.
Reconfiguration Completed.
App Slot Number 1.
RECONFIGURATION SUCCEEDED.
Confirm the root shell prompt returns with no final error.
steps.warning: If an indicator is missing, retain the complete command output and escalate.

steps.title: Run FPGAFactory Test
steps.subtitle: Use the approved production test method for the station.
items: Start the normal FPGAFactory test using the approved station method.
Confirm the final test result is PASS.
If it fails, reconfirm the BMC version, BIOS version, FPGA detection, chip ID, and reconfiguration indicators.
steps.warning: The source WI does not define the FPGAFactory launch command. Do not invent or substitute a command.

steps.title: Document and Escalate
steps.subtitle: Preserve the specific evidence for any unsuccessful result.
items: Firmware mismatch: stop and use the approved BMC/BIOS update process.
No FPGA found: capture the complete fpgadiagnostics -list output.
Driver load error: capture the exact modprobe error.
Reconfiguration failure: capture the command, chip ID, ASMI/RSU messages, PCIe link status, and final error.
FPGAFactory failure: record the failure code or log and reconfirm all prerequisites.
steps.warning: Do not release the tester as passing unless the FPGAFactory result is PASS.
